subject: Database Management System
chapters: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Explain the Three-Schema Architecture of DBMS (Physical/Internal level, Logical/Conceptual level, and External/View level). Define Physical Data Independence and Logical Data Independence. What are the roles and responsibilities of a Database Administrator (DBA)?

Construct an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram for a University Management System showing entities (Student, Department, Course, Instructor, Section), attributes, primary keys, structural cardinality ratios (1:1, 1:N, M:N), participation constraints (total/partial), and weak entity sets. Map the ER diagram into relational schemas.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Explain Enhanced ER (EER) modeling concepts: (a) Specialization and Generalization (Disjoint vs Overlapping, Total vs Partial constraints), (b) Attribute Inheritance, (c) Aggregation, and (d) Categorization / Union Types with clear real-world examples.

Explain fundamental Relational Algebra operations: Selection ($\sigma$), Projection ($\pi$), Cartesian Product ($\times$), Union ($\cup$), Set Difference ($-$), and Rename ($\rho$). Define derived operations: Natural Join ($\bowtie$), Theta Join ($\bowtie_\theta$), Outer Joins (Left, Right, Full $\mathrel{\text{⟕}}, \mathrel{\text{⟖}}, \mathrel{\text{⟗}}$), and Division ($\div$).

Given the relational database schema:
`EMPLOYEE(EmpId, EmpName, Salary, DeptId, SupervisorId)`
`DEPARTMENT(DeptId, DeptName, Location)`
`PROJECT(ProjId, ProjName, DeptId)`
`WORKS_ON(EmpId, ProjId, Hours)`
Write Relational Algebra expressions for: (a) Find names of employees working on project 'AI-Portal', (b) Find employees who work on all projects located in 'Kathmandu', (c) Find employee names earning more than 50,000.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text:
For the same relational database schema above, write SQL queries to:
(a) Find the names of employees who earn higher than the average salary of their own department
(b) Find departments having more than 5 employees with average salary greater than 60,000
(c) List employee names who do not work on any project using `NOT EXISTS` and `NOT IN`
(d) Increase the salary of all employees working on project 'SmartCity' by $10\%$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Explain Views in SQL (Updatable vs Non-updatable views). Explain Stored Procedures and Triggers (Row-level vs Statement-level, Before vs After triggers). Write an SQL trigger that automatically archives deleted employee records into an `Emp_Audit` table.

Define Functional Dependency (FD). State and prove Armstrong's Axioms for FDs (Reflexivity, Augmentation, Transitivity). Explain the algorithm to find the Closure of an Attribute Set $X^+$ with respect to an FD set $F$.
Given a relation $R(A, B, C, D, E, G)$ with functional dependencies $F = \{A \to B, BC \to D, E \to C, D \to A\}$, find: (a) All Candidate Keys of $R$, and (b) Canonical / Minimal Cover of $F$.

Explain First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), Third Normal Form (3NF), and Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF). What are the differences between 3NF and BCNF? A relation $R(A, B, C, D, E)$ has $F = \{A \to BC, CD \to E, B \to D, E \to A\}$. Determine the highest normal form of $R$ and decompose $R$ into BCNF.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Explain the ACID properties of a database transaction (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) and the Transaction State Transition Diagram (Active, Partially Committed, Committed, Failed, Aborted).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: What is Conflict Serializability? Construct a Precedence Graph (Serialization Graph) to test whether the following concurrent schedule is conflict serializable: $S: R_1(A); R_2(A); W_1(A); R_2(B); W_2(A); W_2(B); R_1(B); W_1(B)$. If serializable, find equivalent serial schedule(s).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Transaction Management & Concurrency Control (ACID, Locking)
questions.text: Explain Concurrency Control Anomalies: Dirty Read (Temporary Update), Non-Repeatable Read (Unrepeatable Read), Lost Update, and Phantom Read problems with timing diagrams.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Transaction Management & Concurrency Control (ACID, Locking)
questions.text: Explain Two-Phase Locking (2PL) Protocol. Compare Basic 2PL, Conservative 2PL (Static), Strict 2PL, and Rigorous 2PL. How does Strict 2PL prevent cascading aborts? Does 2PL guarantee freedom from deadlocks?

Explain Deadlock Handling in DBMS: (a) Deadlock Prevention (Wait-Die and Wound-Wait schemes based on timestamps), (b) Deadlock Detection using Wait-For Graph (Cycle detection), and (c) Deadlock Recovery (Victim selection, Rollback, Starvation prevention).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Compare Primary Index, Clustering Index, and Secondary Index (Dense Index vs Sparse Index). Construct a B+ Tree of order $p = 4$ (maximum 3 keys per node) by inserting keys: $5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 85$. Show intermediate splits.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Differentiate between B-Tree and B+ Tree structures. Why are B+ Trees predominantly used for database index structures on disk rather than binary search trees or standard B-trees?

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Explain Log-Based Recovery in DBMS: (a) Deferred Database Modification (NO-UNDO / REDO), (b) Immediate Database Modification (UNDO / REDO), (c) Checkpointing (Fuzzy Checkpointing), and (d) Shadow Paging.
Construct an ER diagram for an Online Hospital Management System showing Patients, Doctors, Appointments, Medical Records, Wards, and Bills with appropriate constraints and relationship sets.

Explain Relational Integrity Constraints: Domain Constraints, Key Constraints, Entity Integrity Constraint (Primary Key not null), and Referential Integrity Constraint (Foreign Key with `ON DELETE CASCADE` and `ON UPDATE SET NULL`).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Database Architecture & Conceptual Data Modeling (ER/EER)
questions.text: Define Lossless Join Decomposition and Dependency-Preserving Decomposition. Test if the decomposition of $R(A, B, C, D, E)$ into $R_1(A, B, C)$ and $R_2(C, D, E)$ with $F = \{A \to BC, CD \to E, B \to D, E \to A\}$ is lossless join and dependency preserving.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Transaction Management & Concurrency Control (ACID, Locking)
questions.text: Explain Timestamp Ordering Protocol for concurrency control. Explain Thomas' Write Rule. Compare Lock-based vs Timestamp-based concurrency control.
Explain ARIES (Algorithms for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics) recovery algorithm: Analysis Pass, Redo Pass, and Undo Pass with Compensation Log Records (CLRs).
Explain Query Processing and Optimization: (a) Parsing and Translation into Query Tree, (b) Heuristic Query Optimization (Push selections and projections down), and (c) Cost-based Optimization.
